page.overview:
What is InGen?

Since 1998, InGen was a subsidiary of Masrani Global Corporation. However, as a result of the Jurassic World Incident, InGen would declare Chapter 11 Bankruptcy at an unknown time before 2027.

Longtime friends John Alfred Hammond and Sir Benjamin Lockwood "dreamed up" the idea to clone dinosaurs from preserved DNA in fossilized amber. Hammond set up a research group, including Lockwood and Dr. Henry Wu to a carry this dream into effect. InGen acquired Isla Sorna and the neighboring Muertes Archipelago in 1982, where they established facilities. They managed to clone a prehistoric animal, a Triceratops horridus, in 1986 and newly born dinosaurs were grown and fed on Isla Sorna. It was here where critical research took place on dinosaurs in a wild environment.

When several dinosaur species were successfully cloned, Hammond started to set up a place where the public could see these animals. In 1983, Hammond began construction on an amphitheatre in San Diego. However, in 1985, Hammond abandoned his idea of the amphitheatre and started to build a far greater Jurassic Park on Isla Nublar, 120 miles off of Costa Rica in 1987. A plant (Serenna veriformans) was also recreated on the island.

In 1993, the park was nearing completion. However, an accident resulted in a 20 million dollar lawsuit from the family of Jophery Brown, scaring the investors and insurance underwriters who feared Jurassic Park was unsafe.

Also known as: International Genetic Technologies.
